title: Adding spatial lookups to RasterField interpolated the user-supplied band index from the lookup tuple straight into the PostGIS SQL template, so a non-integer band index injects SQL.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: In check_raster, lookup.band_lhs and lookup.band_rhs are concatenated directly into the SQL text via '%s, %s' % (template_params['lhs'], lookup.band_lhs) and the same for rhs. These band indices are attacker-influenced: band_rhs is taken verbatim from the lookup tuple (self.rhs[1] in lookups.py:87) and band_lhs from the RasterBandTransform band index (self.lhs.band_index + 1 in lookups.py:79,83).

findings.explanation: In check_raster, lookup.band_lhs and lookup.band_rhs are concatenated directly into the SQL text via '%s, %s' % (template_params['lhs'], lookup.band_lhs) and the same for rhs. These band indices are attacker-influenced: band_rhs is taken verbatim from the lookup tuple (self.rhs[1] in lookups.py:87) and band_lhs from the RasterBandTransform band index (self.lhs.band_index + 1 in lookups.py:79,83). Neither value is validated as an integer nor passed as a bound parameter, so a non-integer value (e.g. a string containing SQL) is interpolated straight into the executed SQL.

evidence.content: SQL injection is a type of attack where a malicious user is able to execute arbitrary SQL code on a database... you should always be careful to properly escape any parameters that the user can control.

findings.suggested_fix: Validate that band_lhs and band_rhs are integers (e.g. assert isinstance(..., int) or cast with int() and reject non-numeric values) before interpolating them into the SQL text, or pass them as bound parameters where the SQL dialect supports it.

findings.explanation: The new process_band_indices() stores self.band_rhs = self.rhs[1] (lookups.py:87), where self.rhs[1] is the band index supplied by the caller in the lookup tuple (e.g. Model.objects.filter(raster__band=2, other__band=3)). This value is later concatenated directly into the SQL text in PostGISOperator.check_raster() via template_params['rhs'] = '%s, %s' % (template_params['rhs'], lookup.band_rhs) (operations.py:66), and the resulting template is rendered into the final SQL string. The band index is never validated to be an integer and is not passed as a bound parameter, so a caller-controlled non-integer value (e.g. a string) is injected verbatim into the SQL statement.

evidence.content: SQL injection is a type of attack where a malicious user is able to execute arbitrary SQL code on a database. This can result in records being deleted or data leakage.

findings.suggested_fix: Validate that the band index is an integer before storing it (e.g. self.band_rhs = int(self.rhs[1]) with a try/except raising ValueError), or pass it as a bound parameter instead of string-concatenating it into the SQL template.
